blocks.content: The Government of India Act of 1935 marked a second milestone towards a completely responsible government in India and provided the structural framework of the Constitution.

rows: Proposed Dyarchy at Center & All-India Federation
Granted limited franchise based on property, tax, or education
Extended franchise to about 10% of the total population

items: Regulating Act of 1773 provided for the establishment of a Supreme Court at Calcutta in 1774.
Dyarchy was introduced in the provinces by the Act of 1919, whereas provincial autonomy replaced it under the Act of 1935.
The office of the Secretary of State for India was created under the Government of India Act of 1858.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Regulating Act of 1773 designated the Governor of Bengal as the Governor-General of Bengal and laid the foundation of central administration.
Pitt's India Act of 1784 established a system of double government by distinguishing between commercial and political functions of the Company.
The Charter Act of 1833 made the Governor-General of Bengal the Governor-General of India and centralized all legislative powers.
The Government of India Act of 1858 abolished the East India Company and transferred powers of government, territories, and revenues to the British Crown.
The Government of India Act of 1935 contemplated an All-India Federation and served as the major structural blueprint for the Indian Constitution.
